verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: mark-ready.mjs:291-300 contains a bare `catch {}` that converts any failure of the `commits/{sha}/check-runs` read into `allPassed:false` with no log line, which flows to gates[2] (line 313) and `process.exit(1)` with the verdict string (line 329). The workflow's exit-1 branch (agent-review-panel.yml:1539-1542) records `outcome=gates-unsatisfied` and lets the promote job SUCCEED, and the `stalled` net only pages on `needs.promote.result == 'failure'` (line 2330, comment 2211-2212 scopes it to exit 2), so no page fires. mark-ready.mjs is invoked from exactly one place (line 1508) with no scheduled retry, and set-state reconcile only reconciles labels — nothing re-attempts promotion for that SHA. The asymmetry is real: gate 1's catch (175-189) exits 2 for the identical class of read failure with a comment naming the silent-draft-forever hazard, gate 1b's catch (274-281) still claims exit 1 "matches gate 1", and set-state.mjs:238-245 treats the same check-runs read failure as `complete = false` (honored at 269-272), confirming the intended convention. Swallowing a transient API failure into a false gate refusal is error-handling mis-handling in the Correctness lane; no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) applies.

finding.summary: Gate 1b re-reads (pins) the head SHA but never re-reads the base ref — a base retarget landing between the base check and the file listing empties the list and the gate passes
finding.evidence: `ranBaseCiDefinition` reads `pr.baseRefName` from the snapshot taken at line 137-143 and compares it to `defaultBranch()` (line 231-237), then fetches `pulls/N/files` (line 239), then re-reads `headRefOid` (line 246) explicitly "so it covers the whole window in which the evidence was gathered". But `pulls/N/files` is computed by GitHub against the PR's base AT REQUEST TIME, and the base is never re-read. An author who flips the base from `main` to a branch that already carries the gutted CI definition after line 232 but before line 239 gets an empty/clean file list, the head-pin at line 246 still matches (no push happened), and gate 1b returns true. The gate's own comment (a) says the base is author-controlled and mutable, which is exactly why it is checked — yet the mutable-field pinning treatment given to the head is not given to the base. Fix: re-read `baseRefName` alongside `headRefOid` after the file listing.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree: `pr.baseRefName` is read exactly once (mark-ready.mjs:142) and compared to the live default branch at mark-ready.mjs:243-249; the file list is then fetched from `pulls/N/files` (mark-ready.mjs:211 via 251), which GitHub computes against the PR's base at request time; only `headRefOid` is re-pinned afterwards (mark-ready.mjs:258-264). No base re-read exists anywhere — grep across scripts/ shows `baseRefName` only at mark-ready.mjs:142,244,246 plus unrelated eval/extract-corpus.mjs and test fixtures (mark-ready.test.mjs:431,444). No outer guard compensates: the sole caller, the promote job at .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1494-1550, only branches on the exit code and performs no base assertion, and gates 1 and 2 (mark-ready.mjs:193, 302) key off headRefOid, which a base retarget does not move. So a retarget landing between line 244 and line 251 empties the hit list, the head pin at 259 still matches, and gate 1b returns true — a TOCTOU/ordering defect that breaks the pinning invariant the function's own comment (mark-ready.mjs:238-242) states. Correctness lane (races/ordering, broken invariant); impact is a fail-open of the CI-definition gate = major. I found no counterexample.

finding.summary: `ciRunToRerun` can select a run that is not the run gate 1 reads, producing a panel round that can never promote and no further admissible panel event
finding.evidence: `ciRunToRerun` returns the newest COMPLETED run, while `ciConclusion` (gate 1, mark-ready.mjs:178) returns the newest run by id regardless of status, and the panel's `ci` job (agent-review-panel.yml:300-336) reads the TRIGGERING run. When a head SHA carries two runs (close/reopen files a second `pull_request` run — the docstring at checks.mjs:165-170 acknowledges this) and the newer one is still in flight, `@claude rerun` re-runs the older finished run. That emits `completed` with `run_attempt > 1`, which the panel gate admits; the panel's `ci` job sees that run succeed and promote runs; but mark-ready's gate 1 reads the NEWER (in-flight) run, gets `null`, and exits 1 ("leaving as draft"). The newer run's own `completed` event arrives with `run_attempt == 1` and is REFUSED by the panel gate (agent-review-panel.yml:168-169), so no further panel round is admitted and the PR sits as a draft — the exact failure mode the comment at agent-review-panel.yml:1454-1461 exists to prevent. The docstring's claim that "gate 1 reads whichever ends up newest when it next runs" assumes a next panel round that the gate does not admit.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present in the tree. `ciRunToRerun` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:231-233) selects the newest COMPLETED run, while gate 1's `ciConclusion` (checks.mjs:193-197, called at mark-ready.mjs:190) selects the newest run by id regardless of status and returns null when it is in flight — so with two runs on one head SHA (a documented, unguarded case per checks.test.mjs:607-636 and mark-ready.test.mjs:500-507) `@claude rerun` (agent-rerun.yml:200-205, the inline mirror) re-runs a different run than gate 1 reads. The panel's `ci` job polls only the TRIGGERING run (agent-review-panel.yml:300), so it can report success while promote's mark-ready reads the still-in-flight newer run, exits 1 and logs "leaving as draft" — the exact outcome the comment at agent-review-panel.yml:1453-1461 says produces no page and no re-run. The docstring's assumption of a later round (checks.mjs:213-219) is not honored: the newer run's eventual `completed` event carries run_attempt == 1 and is refused by the gate (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169), and the round its `requested` event started shares the `active` concurrency group with the re-run's round and is cancelled by `cancel-in-progress: true` (agent-review-panel.yml:115-118). No guard elsewhere prevents issuing a rerun while a newer run is in flight, so I cannot refute on any named ground.
